Lending assets under management witnessed a robust 32% growth to Rs 2.34 lakh crore, while shares gained 1.75% on the Bombay Stock Exchange.

Varun Beverages Q3 Profit Up 14% to ₹831 Cr; Revenue Jumps 33%
Varun Beverages Q3 results: Profit rises 13.5% to ₹830.6 cr, revenue up 33%
items.summary:
Varun Beverages Ltd, PepsiCo's largest franchise bottler, on Friday reported a 13.54 per cent on-year increase in consolidated net profit at Rs 830.6 crore for the September quarter of 2026, driven by double-digit volume growth in India and international markets.
The company, which follows the calendar year as its financial year, had posted a net profit of Rs 731.51 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Varun Beverages Ltd (VBL).
Revenue from operations was up 33.3 per cent to Rs 6,815.58 crore in the September quarter of 2026. It stood at Rs 5,112.43 crore in the corresponding quarter of the last year.
Total expenses of VBL were up 35.77 per cent to Rs 5,880.55 crore in the September quarter.
VBL's total consolidated income, which includes other income, in the September quarter was at Rs 6,935.44 crore, up 31.85 per cent.
On a standalone basis, which primarily includes India sales, VBL's revenue from operations was up 24.75 per cent

items.summary:
Varun Beverages Ltd, PepsiCo's largest franchise bottler, on Friday reported a 13.54 per cent on-year increase in consolidated net profit at Rs 830.6 crore for the September quarter of 2026, driven by double-digit volume growth in India and international markets.
The company, which follows the calendar year as its financial year, had posted a net profit of Rs 731.51 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Varun Beverages Ltd (VBL).
Revenue from operations was up 33.3 per cent to Rs 6,815.58 crore in the September quarter of 2026. It stood at Rs 5,112.43 crore in the corresponding quarter of the last year.
Total expenses of VBL were up 35.77 per cent to Rs 5,880.55 crore in the September quarter.
VBL's total consolidated income, which includes other income, in the September quarter was at Rs 6,935.44 crore, up 31.85 per cent.
On a standalone basis, which primarily includes India sales, VBL's revenue from operations was up 24.75 per cent

items.title: Vedanta lines up $25 bn investment over next three years for organic growth
items.summary:
The Vedanta Group has lined up USD 25 billion in investments over the next three years to expand capacities across its existing businesses through organic growth and brownfield expansions, a top company official said.
Vedanta founder and chairman Anil Agarwal, who was in the city on Wednesday, said the conglomerate would focus on its existing assets for growth, while remaining open to acquiring public sector assets if opportunities arise.
"Current capex plans are for organic growth in aluminium, copper, zinc, oil and gas. All will be brownfield expansions," he said.
"We are going to invest around USD 25 billion," Agarwal said.
The capital expenditure would also support Vedanta's ambition to become one of the world's largest mining companies in critical metals, and emerge as a leading silver producer within three to four years, he said.
The group, which comprises 10 major companies, aims to grow its overall business from USD 30 billion to USD 50 billion within three years, Agarwal
